correctness.rationale: Ordinary reflexive-transitive root modalities cannot count duplicated terminal-cluster support sets or color multiplicities within clusters. A matching-support back-and-forth bisimulation gives modal invariance. Conversely depth-one δ_S detects terminal support S, and depth-two ◇δ_S, with an extra P_b witness when S is the global support T, separates each different support family; root color a and T are directly definable. Thus root types are pairs (a,H), where H is a nonempty set of at most t feasible color supports; M=q Σ_{j=1}^{min(t,N)} C(N,j), N=Σ_{j=1}^{min(s,q)} C(q,j), q=2^k. The root-fixing wreath product S_s wr S_t sees histograms with C(s+q−1,q−1) possible types and their multisets; E=q C(t+Hcount−1,Hcount−1). Every modal class receives an invariant orbit measure, so the observation map is onto the M-simplex with affine kernel E−M. Collision if and only if k≥1 and (s≥3 or t≥3): vary a two-color histogram inside a cluster (s≥3) or duplicate support multiplicities (t≥3). k=0 and (t,s)=(1,1) depth boundaries checked; t→∞ asymptotic follows the finite support count. Independent literal world-valuation enumeration checked small q,t,s against depth-zero/two signatures and wreath histogram orbits. Finite checks corroborate, rather than prove, all-parameter bisimulation and counting.

value.rationale: The exact information loss in learning automorphism-invariant valuation distributions from ordinary modal observations is a motivated identifiability problem. The four-world strict-loss onset, full simplex-image dimensions and sharp depth-two test give a complete quantitative answer for a natural finite star-of-S5-clusters S4 family. The computation is not a mere relabeling of generic bisimulation invariance; it resolves whether distinct symmetric priors are distinguishable by any permitted modal event.
